B-1.why: Graham has been covered by Halberd's group plan on his current employment since 2009, so he enrolls in Part B in the special enrollment period (42 CFR 406.24, 407.20) with no penalty months (408.24). Enrolling in October, while still covered, he may start on 1 November 2026, the day after the group coverage ends: no gap and no month paid twice (406.24(e)). Waiting for COBRA's 18 months to run out, as the broker urges, closes the 8 months; he would enroll in the January 2029 general period with 27 months uncovered, a 20% penalty: $40.58 a month at 2026's $202.90, $487 a year for as long as he has Part B

traps.B-2: Lena's group coverage on her own current employment ended on 31 January 2025; her retiree coverage is not current employment, so her 8 months ended in September 2025 (406.24, 407.20). Submitting a special-period enrollment for her claims coverage she does not have; her way in is the general enrollment period, from 1 January 2027

E-4471.why: Form CMS-L564, Section B completed by Halberd, is the proof of Graham's group coverage on current employment that his special-period enrollment needs; HR completes it within 5 business days. Counted as an item at $0: it is a step to the enrollment, not money

traps.D-2: Theo is 24 and not eligible for Medicare: an L564 for him supports no enrollment

traps.T-1: COBRA is not coverage based on current employment and does not extend Graham's 8 months; with Medicare it pays after Medicare and may pay only what it would have after Part B. $812 a month for coverage that does not replace Part B
traps.T-3: Lena is not on Halberd's group plan: she has her own retiree coverage, and COBRA would open no Part B period for her either

T-2.why: Theo, 24, loses the group coverage on 31 October; continuing it under COBRA is the family's choice for him, and harmless here

traps.T-1: Graham's group coverage runs to 31 October; cancelling it today leaves him uncovered for the rest of October, before Part B starts
traps.T-2: Theo's group coverage runs to 31 October; cancelling it today leaves him uncovered
traps.T-3: Lena's retiree plan is her only coverage beside Part A until Part B starts in 2027, and a retiree who leaves it may not rejoin

traps.M-4: A $299 fee to file forms that are free and can be filed online, with the employer's L564 that HR completes on request

M-2.why: Replying to the insurer's notice is harmless

M-3.why: Replying to the broker is harmless, whatever the reply says

M-5.why: Telling Lena why she must wait for January is helpful
